paragraphs: By way of introduction, my name is Joshua Chappell. My intent is to apply for the AI Training & Enablement Specialist position at Guild Mortgage. I feel I have a lot of immediate value I can bring to your organization.

Your posting asks for someone who can translate technical AI capabilities into practical skills for different teams and skill levels. I have taught technical tools to beginners for years. As a teacher, I elevated 80+ beginner students to 95% camera operation proficiency through hands-on curriculum and assessment. On YouTube, I reached over a million people teaching post-production techniques. I know how to break a complex tool into steps a beginner can follow, and how to check that the lesson stuck.

I bring hands-on AI experience to your rollouts. At Charter One, I used Claude agentic coding to build content workflows that cut production times in half. I work in ChatGPT, Runway, Kling, Veo, and ElevenLabs, so the examples I teach come from real production work. I maintained an organized library of video assets in Frame.io and Dropbox, reducing search and retrieval time by over 50%, and I will hold your knowledge base to the same standard: accurate, current, and easy to find. My Master's in Marketing, with a Marketing Analytics specialization, supports the measurement side of the role, from adoption and proficiency to what the feedback says to fix next.
I appreciate that you value customer service, integrity, respect, collaboration, learning, and excellence; these are all values that I strive to emulate.
Thank you for taking the time out of your busy day to read my letter. I look forward to the opportunity of doing an interview with you.

reference.jd_text:
**Guild Mortgage Company**, closing loans and opening doors since 1960. As a mortgage banking firm we are dedicated to serving the home owner/buyer. Our goal is to provide affordable home financing for our customers, utilizing the best terms available while providing a level of professionalism and service unsurpassed in the lending industry.

**Position Summary**

The AI Training & Enablement Specialist owns an assigned function within the organization's AI training and enablement work, for example training, departmental enablement, communications, adoption, or an emerging program or platform. Working under general direction, the Specialist independently assesses needs within that function, designs and builds the enablement solutions and learning experiences it requires, creates original content, and evaluates and improves effectiveness over time. The role requires the consistent exercise of independent judgment: translating technical AI capabilities for the intended audience, selecting the approach and format, and deciding how the work is structured and measured. The Specialist applies responsible AI, data privacy, and compliance standards to everything the role designs and delivers.

**Compensation**

This role is an exempt position with a Targeted Salary Range of 82,506 to $118,345 annually.

Compensation at Guild is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to local and federal minimum wage requirements, education, level of experience, and applicant's geographical location.

**Essential Functions**

- Design, develop, and maintain the enablement programs, learning journeys, and resources for the assigned function, tailored to different business units and skill levels.
- Translate technical AI capabilities into practical enablement by partnering with AI Engineers, Data Scientists, Product, and IT, using independent judgment to decide what to convey and how.
- Design and facilitate workshops, webinars, hands-on labs, office hours, and other sessions, adapting content and delivery based on audience needs and feedback.
- Assess needs across teams and determine the priorities, gaps, and approach needed to close them, aligned with business goals and AI maturity levels.
- Create original content and resources, such as playbooks, FAQs, job aids, guides, tutorials, communications, and assessments, exercising professional judgment over structure, format, and modality.
- Build and maintain the knowledge base for the assigned function, keeping content accurate, current, and easy to find.
- Incorporate responsible AI, data-handling, and compliance standards into the work, using judgment to tailor guidance to each audience.
- Stay current on new AI tools and features being introduced across the organization and determine what updates the assigned function needs as a result.
- Analyze AI usage trends and audience feedback to identify what is working, diagnose adoption barriers, and improve effectiveness.
- Deliver the enablement components of AI rollouts, including readiness, reinforcement, and launch materials.
- Define and track measures of effectiveness (adoption, proficiency, satisfaction, question themes) and use the findings to improve the work.
- Stay current with AI trends, technologies, and enablement best practices to keep the work relevant and effective.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**

- Bachelors Degree directly related to the position or equivalent, preferred Instructional Design, Education, Communications, Information Systems, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, or related field (or equivalent experience).
- Masters Degree directly related to the position or equivalent, preferred Instructional Design, Learning Sciences, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), Data/AI-related discipline, or related field.
- Minimum three years' experience in training, enablement, instructional design, technical writing, customer education, or a related function, including experience supporting adoption of digital tools in a fast-changing environment.
- Preferred: relevant certs in learning design, facilitation, Microsoft 365, or AI tooling.
- Ability to organize and manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
- Ability to work well independently or within a team.
- Strong interpersonal and customer service skills Excellent interpersonal communication skills required.
- Must be able to handle confidential matters with discretion.
- Experience supporting enterprise tool rollouts (Microsoft 365/Copilot, knowledge platforms, workflow tools).
- Exposure to regulated environments (financial services preferred) and training aligned to policy/compliance requirements.
- Experience building and maintaining knowledge bases (SharePoint/Teams or similar).
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills required.
- Highly organized and detail-oriented; ability to work in a fast-paced, metrics-driven environment required.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, Word, Excel, Wiki, collaborative cloud-based programs, and third-party software applications required.
- **Commitment to company values.**
- Customer Service - Proactive attention to each person
- Integrity - Do and say what's right
- Respect - Treat others with dignity
- Collaboration - Listen and work together
- Learning - Seek knowledge and strive for improvement
- Excellence - Deliver the unexpected

**Supervision**

- Job Scope: Responsible for understanding the department/functional area objectives and goals and how own job contributes to achievement of these goals; may recommend changes and enhancements based on analysis and evaluation of circumstances.
- Complexity: General precedents may exist for most problems; conducts independent research/analysis to identify the appropriate approach.
- Impact: Decisions and actions primarily impact own work with limited impact on peers in their area, contributes as team member rather than leader.
- Interaction/Supervision: Acts as a mentor/guide to less experienced professional contributor staff in a similar role; works independently and only under general direction; guided by professional standards, desired outcomes, and project plan specifications

**Requirements**

Physical: Work is primarily sedentary; mobility in an office setting.

Manual Dexterity: Frequent use of computer keyboard and mouse.

Audio/Visual: Ability to accurately interpret sounds and associated meanings at a volume consistent with interpersonal conversation. Regularly required to accurately perceive, distinguish and interpret information received visually and through audio, e.g., words, numbers and other data broadcasted aloud/viewed on a screen, as well as print and other media.

Environmental: Office environment - moderate noise, no substantial exposure to adverse environmental conditions.

Mental: Learn new tasks, remember processes, maintain focus, complete tasks independently, and make timely decisions in the context of a workflow.

This role requires effective adaptation to workplace stressors, including customer service complaints, security responsibilities, and competing priorities. Must be able to adhere to process protocol. Must be able to apply established protocols in a timely manner.

Schedules: Work is primarily performed during the business week, Monday - Friday.

Travel: 5% or less

Guild offers a pleasant work environment, competitive compensation and excellent benefits package; including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, AD&D, LTD and 401(k) with employer match.

Guild Mortgage Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

REQ#: AITRA018532

Equal Opportunity Employer

This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws.
For further information, please review the Know Your Rights notice from the Department of Labor.

research.overview: Guild Mortgage Company is a mortgage banking firm that says it has been in business since 1960. This report rests on two kinds of evidence, both from Dice: the full posting for the AI Training & Enablement Specialist role, and Dice's list of other Guild openings. All of those openings share one Dice employer ID (80184063), and the AI posting under that ID names Guild Mortgage Company. I could not gather any employee reviews. The web search limit for this run was used up before my first search, the Indeed connector failed with a rate-limit error (-32429), and Glassdoor and Reddit cannot be opened from here. That means I have no ratings, no review counts, no employee quotes, and nothing on teams. Layoffs, leadership turnover, return-to-office policy, and pay complaints are unchecked. The role sits in AI training and enablement, not a marketing or creative team. On paper it is a remote, US-based individual contributor job, exempt, with a posted range of $82,506 to $118,345. Since September 4, 2026, Guild has posted at least 10 tech and data roles on Dice, and every one is listed as remote.

glassdoor.summary: Not checked. The web search limit for this run was used up before any search ran, and Glassdoor cannot be opened from this environment. I am not reporting a rating or review count. Check Glassdoor yourself before interviewing, and filter for corporate, IT, or training roles if the site allows it.

indeed.summary: Not checked. The Indeed connector failed to connect (rate-limit error -32429), and no web search could run, so I have no Indeed company rating or reviews. Try the Indeed company page yourself, or rerun this research once the connector is working.

reddit.summary: Not checked. The web search limit was used up and Reddit cannot be opened from this environment, so I found no threads. I did not invent any.

pros.point: The job is fully remote in the US. Dice lists it as Remote, the schedule is Monday to Friday, and travel is 5% or less.
The pay range is published. It is an exempt role with a target salary of $82,506 to $118,345 a year.
The posting lists a standard benefits package: medical, dental, vision, life insurance, AD&D, long-term disability, and a 401(k) with employer match.

Guild is hiring for technology this fall. Since September 4, 2026, it has posted a Lead Software Engineer, Principal Integration Architect, Senior Cloud Architect, Manager of DevOps, Senior Data Analyst, Senior Data Governance Analyst, Senior System Administrator for Microsoft Platforms, and Manager of IT QA. Dice lists all of them as Remote. That points to a working remote setup for corporate tech staff and to spending on tech and data. I did not open the full descriptions for these roles.

The role comes with ownership and room for judgment. The Specialist owns a function, designs its programs and content, sets the measures of success (adoption, proficiency, satisfaction), works under general direction, and mentors less experienced staff.

An AI team appears to exist already. The posting says the role partners with AI Engineers, Data Scientists, Product, and IT, and that it delivers the enablement parts of AI rollouts, including Microsoft 365 and Copilot.

cons.point: The salary Dice shows can mislead. The listing displays $118,345 a year, but that is the top of the $82,506 to $118,345 range. The posting also says pay depends partly on the applicant's location, so a remote hire in a lower-cost area may get a lower offer.

The scope is a mid-level individual contributor job. The posting says decisions 'primarily impact own work with limited impact on peers' and that the person 'contributes as team member rather than leader.'

The actual assignment is not defined. The role owns 'an assigned function,' and the examples given are training, departmental enablement, communications, adoption, or an emerging program. The day-to-day work could vary widely depending on which one you get.

This is a regulated, compliance-heavy setting. Responsible AI, data privacy, and compliance standards apply to everything the role produces. The posting describes a 'fast-paced, metrics-driven environment' and names stressors including complaints, security responsibilities, and competing priorities.

The tools are Microsoft-centered: Microsoft 365, Copilot, and knowledge bases in SharePoint or Teams. If most of your hands-on AI work has been in other tools, expect some ramp-up, and be ready to show you can move between tools.

The benefits list leaves out paid time off, holidays, parental leave, bonus or incentive pay, and tuition or certification support. The posting alone cannot tell you how these compare to other employers.

red_flags: Employee sentiment is unknown. No Glassdoor, Indeed, or Reddit data was collected: the web search limit was used up, the Indeed connector failed, and the sites are blocked here. Read reviews yourself before an offer, with attention to corporate and IT roles and to anything from 2025 to 2026.

Layoffs, leadership turnover, and return-to-office policy were not checked. Ask whether Guild has cut staff in the last two years, how corporate and IT headcount has changed, and whether remote status for this role is permanent.

Guild's VP and Chief Information Security Officer role is open (posted September 14, 2026). Ask whether it is a new role or a backfill, and who sets AI governance and data-handling policy in the meantime.
Guild has posted 10 remote tech and data roles on Dice since September 4, 2026. That may mean growth or it may mean turnover. Ask which roles are new headcount.

Questions for the interview: Which function would this role own? Who does it report to? How big is the AI and enablement team? Which AI tools are live today, and which are planned? How will adoption and proficiency be measured in the first 6 to 12 months? Is there a location-based pay adjustment, and where would an offer land in the $82,506 to $118,345 range?
research.bottom_line: Going by the posting, this is a sound remote role. The range is published ($82,506 to $118,345), the benefits are standard, you would own a defined area of work, and an AI team with engineers and data scientists is already in place. Guild's fall 2026 hiring of remote tech and data roles suggests the company is investing in technology. The main gap is employee sentiment: no Glassdoor, Indeed, or Reddit data could be gathered in this run, so culture, layoffs, management quality, and pay satisfaction are unknown. Before accepting an offer, check reviews yourself. In interviews, pin down which function you would own, where in the range the offer would land given your location, and whether the role will stay remote.
